W-01.note: M1 polysemy set for 'temperate': A climate and B teetotal are the literal/etymological senses, C is the idiom-bound one; D 'measured' is the extended sense SAT tests of tone or judgment

W-02.note: M1 same headword as W-01 in meaning form; D 'slow to reach a verdict' is not a sense of the word at all (pure decoy), A and C are literal/idiomatic; B is the extended sense

W-03.note: M3 odd one out: reversible/accidental/predictable are all contingency properties, gradual is the only rate property - but odd-one-out is as often the distractor writer's slip as the key; low confidence

W-04.note: M1 polysemy set for 'economy': C is the primary sense, A the etymological one, D a register error; B 'sparing use of means' is the extended sense (economy of expression)

W-05.note: M4 hedging - provisional is the only qualified option and D 'generous' is off-dimension; but C 'incontrovertible' is equally arguable on the register channel, so the two channels disagree

W-06.note: M1 polysemy set for 'color' as verb: A literal, B and D physical/affective senses; C 'bias the impression of' is the figurative sense used of evidence or accounts

W-07.note: M5 collocation: claims in academic prose are 'contested'; dispositive and premonitory are the exotic furniture. Register channel would pick C instead, so this is a coin flip dressed as a reason

W-08.note: M4 hedging: conjectural is the tentative one; coeval is the rare decoy, successive/unremarkable the plain ones

W-09.note: M5/specificity: 'verbatim transcripts' is the one technically precise option; B would win on the hedging channel instead - channels conflict

W-10.note: M1 polysemy set for 'address': A, B, D are the three everyday senses; C 'skill in handling situations' is the archaic/rare sense, which is exactly the one such an item exists to test

W-11.note: M1 polysemy set for 'homely': D is the US primary sense and therefore the distractor; B and C are surface re-readings of the morphology; A is the British/literary sense

W-12.note: M1: options are senses of accretion/accrual; B 'financial gains' is the primary/literal sense and so the trap, D off-dimension; A 'gradual accumulations' is the extended sense

W-13.note: M5 collocation - 'chronicle the changes' is the standard academic verb and the only one that entails a record over time; instruct/publicize/discern are plausible in many frames

W-14.note: M2 near-synonym elimination: spareness and frugality are interchangeable in almost any slot, so neither can be a unique key; B 'machinery' is an off-dimension decoy; C 'prosperity' survives

W-15.note: M3 odd one out: premature/incomplete/unwarranted all say the reasoning does not go far enough; 'circular' is the only named structural fallacy and the only term of art

W-16.note: M3: A, C, D are all strategic or culpable acts; B is the only sincere reading, and 'genuine' is an intensifier no distractor writer needs

W-17.note: accommodation is the SAT-favoured compromise word; imposition/open rivalry are the two poles and negotiation a near-synonym of C, which weakens rather than supports the pick

W-18.note: M2+M5: literal and exacting are near-synonyms in a translation frame and D 'idiomatic' is literal's antonym-pole decoy; 'faithful' is the standard collocate and the only one not paired

W-19.note: register: contrition is the most formal and least common of the four; no independent support

W-20.note: M4 hedging: equivocal is the only option about indeterminacy; the other three are all judgments of worth or origin
